Illustration of the three bee castes side-by-side for comparison. Left: Queen bee, showing a very long, pointed abdomen extending past her wings. Middle: Drone bee, showing a bulky, stout body with huge eyes meeting at the top of the head. Right: Worker bee, showing a smaller, compact body with a pollen basket on her hind leg.

A side-by-side comparison of a traditional and modern hive. Left: A woven cylindrical basket hive tied to the branch of a tree with ropes. Right: A wooden Kenyan Top-Bar hive standing on four legs, with its sloped lid slightly open showing wooden bars arranged neatly across the top.

A bee-keeper in full safety gear working at a wooden Langstroth hive. The person is wearing a white coverall (bee suit), a wide-brimmed hat with a mesh veil covering the face, and thick yellow leather gloves. In their right hand, they hold a metal smoker with a bellows, gently puffing smoke over a wooden hive frame they are holding with their left hand. A metal hive tool rests on the lid of the wooden hive box nearby.
